{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVIgqiM8AAAABXGBNew", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm76XzhAp2jQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm76X", "number": 7, "title": "Evaluate the existing 100-step LoRA adapter on all 500 MBPP test problems", "body": "## Problem

The first measured 100-step LoRA experiment on Qwen3-4B produced a small change on 50 MBPP test problems:

| Model | Correct | Pass@1 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base (no adapter) | 38/50 | 76% |
| After 100-step LoRA | 39/50 | 78% |

Two items changed from incorrect to correct, and one from correct to incorrect. The measured +2 percentage points (+1 problem) is too small and the sample too limited to conclude that LoRA reliably improves code-generation ability. During that run, Docker container startup delays affected scoring; the reported numbers came from rescoring the saved generations under consistent conditions.

We need a larger **paired evaluation on the complete 500-problem official MBPP test split** before trying different training-step counts.

## Expected outcome

Provide a reproducible, documented way to evaluate the **same existing base checkpoint and existing 100-step LoRA adapter** on all MBPP test task IDs 11–510, score them under consistent execution conditions, and compare base-versus-adapted pass@1, net changes, and per-task transitions.

Reuse the repository's existing MLX-LM inference, dataset preparation, Docker sandbox, and comparison tooling where possible; make only focused changes required to make the 500-problem evaluation reliable. Keep downloads, model weights, adapters, generated code, and result files local and ignored by Git.

## Context

- Related: Issue #5 and PR #6 introduced the Qwen/MBPP end-to-end experiment.
- The current `configs/experiment.json` defaults to `eval_size: 50`, with instructions in README to copy the config, set `eval_size: 500`, and use fresh dataset and result paths.
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507` at the pinned revision in the repository, converted to MLX; "base" means that checkpoint without the experiment's adapter.
- Training: reuse the 100-iteration LoRA adapter and its recorded training metadata. **Do not train a new 300/500-step adapter or vary hyperparameters in this Issue.** Those are possible follow-ups after the full evaluation.
- Scoring caveat: Docker startup latency was observed to affect the prior 50-question measurements. A timeout that starts before the container/code is ready can incorrectly mark correct programs as failures; scoring must remain bounded and safe.
- The repository follows the [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), including English Issue/PR content.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Add or document a **copy-and-run 500-problem procedure** starting with the existing environment, unchanged base model, and existing 100-step adapter. Use a copied experiment configuration with `eval_size: 500` and fresh ignored data/output paths; do not overwrite the original 50-problem results.
- [ ] Ensure the generated evaluation manifest contains **exactly the official MBPP test IDs 11–510 once each**, with no overlap with training/validation IDs, and preserve the data-source revision, hashes, prompt/test format, and seed. Add lightweight assertions/tests as needed.
- [ ] Evaluate **both base and LoRA-adapted versions** against those same 500 ordered examples, identical prompt/decoding parameters and Docker scoring image/resource limits. Keep the model revision and existing adapter fixed; record sufficient metadata to confirm both runs are comparable.
- [ ] Inspect Docker startup/readiness timing and code-execution time accounting. Ensure slow container startup is not silently counted as a model's code-execution failure; preserve a bounded startup failure mode, a separate bounded execution deadline, isolation, cleanup, and fail-closed infrastructure error handling. If the existing implementation already satisfies these criteria, document and verify it instead of rewriting it.
- [ ] Provide a way to **rescore saved generations without re-generating them** under the identical scorer settings if infrastructure timing necessitates rescoring, without changing the generated code. Make sure comparison rejects inconsistent or incomplete scoring runs.
- [ ] Report the two pass@1 results as successes/500 and percentages, the signed percentage-point difference, and counts of **fail→pass, pass→fail, unchanged-pass, unchanged-fail**. Identify task IDs whose outcomes changed. Include a short interpretation acknowledging sampling/pretraining contamination and that this single paired benchmark does not prove a general improvement.
- [ ] Add focused automated, hardware-independent tests for any changed splitting, scoring startup/execution boundaries, reuse of generated outputs, provenance comparison, and outcome counts. Run applicable tests, syntax/dependency/Markdown/whitespace checks before merge; honestly document performed and unperformed real-device runs.
- [ ] Update or add concise README/docs commands and output descriptions, preserve existing project instructions, and propose an Issue-linked PR targeting `main`. Do not commit datasets, model/adapter weights, generated responses, or bulky benchmark artifacts.

## Optional validation

- Execute the complete 500 + 500 generations and scoring on a Mac with sufficient memory and Docker available, reuse the locally saved 100-step LoRA adapter, and summarize **actual measured** results. This is useful but is not a mandatory pre-merge gate for an agent without access to the model, local adapter, or suitable hardware; in that case, document the exact commands and report it as not performed.
- Recheck the original 50 task IDs under the new consistent scorer settings to diagnose timing-related changes; never present the 50 and 500 scores as an identical sample.
- Repeat runs or use an independent held-out problem set in a later Issue for robustness.

## Required post-merge verification

None required by this Issue: merging does not trigger a deployment or benchmark run. Do not claim that 500-problem outcomes were measured unless the actual evaluation was run and recorded.
